selectedDefects.issueTitle: In list mode, can't select the last book if one is already selected.
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the fixed select-mode action bar overlays the bottom of the shelf because the virtualised list reserves a constant 34px footer regardless of the bar's real height, so the last book row sits underneath it. That makes the trigger a hit test rather than a state assertion: a click has to be delivered at the last row's real window coordinates through the WebKitGTK webview, and on the affected build the action bar receives it instead of the book. Dispatching a synthetic DOM click on the row element would hit the row and would not reproduce, which is exactly the distinction the Tauri adapter exists to make. The observable is the selected-count in the action bar, which does not increment on the affected build
remaining: build the Tauri Linux artifact at both revisions in the x86_64 worker with webkit2gtk-4.1 and libappindicator present
seed a deterministic library of enough local epub files that the last row falls under the action bar at the worker's fixed window size
pin the window geometry, because the defect depends on the last row being within the bar's height of the viewport bottom
prove the neighbouring legal behaviour: selecting a non-last book with the same click path succeeds on the affected build

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the annotation index is memoized, so a highlight deleted in place still sits in its section bucket and is re-drawn as an orphaned overlay on the next render pass. Reproducing it needs a real text selection inside the foliate iframe, that is a press, drag, and release across glyph coordinates in the rendered book view rather than a programmatic Range, then the popup's highlight and delete actions in quick succession. The overlay is drawn by the reader, not by the DOM the host controls, so the observable is a rendered annotation overlay that persists after deletion. This exercises the Tauri adapter's pointer-drag path and its ability to observe inside a nested browsing context
remaining: build the Tauri Linux artifact at both revisions
seed a fixed epub and a fixed reading position so the same glyph range is selectable every run
establish that the delete must land before the index is rebuilt, and decide whether that ordering is deterministic enough for a three-run reproduction or whether it needs an explicit wait
confirm the orphaned overlay is observable without instrumenting the application, otherwise record the observation method as a corpus property

selectedDefects.issueTitle: BUG: Can't jump to chapters with special characters (like &) from table of contents.
selectedDefects.whySuitable: a persisted nav cache written by an older build stores the ampersand chapter's TOC href percent-encoded, which no longer resolves against the decoded manifest, so clicking that TOC entry silently does nothing. The fix bumps BOOK_NAV_VERSION so the stale cache is recomputed. This is a persisted-state defect across an application lifecycle rather than an input path, which makes it complementary to the other two readest selections: it exercises the Tauri adapter's ownership of the application data directory between launches, and the observable is the reader's section indicator failing to change after a real click on a TOC row
remaining: build the Tauri Linux artifact at both revisions
author an epub containing a chapter whose href carries a reserved character, and confirm the encoded form is what the affected build persists
produce the pre-fix cache honestly: open the book once on the affected build to write the version 3 cache, then relaunch, rather than hand-writing a cache file
decide whether the fixed control needs the same seeded stale cache, since the fix is precisely the invalidation of it

selectedDefects.issueTitle: 添加供应商页面 搜索预设后无法点击选中搜索结果
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the click-outside handler is bound to a container ref that wraps only the search input row, not the result list below it, so pressing the mouse on a search result fires the outside-click path and clears the search before the click completes. The result is never selected. This can only be reproduced by a real pointer sequence, mousedown then mouseup on the result at its window coordinates. A single synthetic click event, or any harness that jumps straight to the element's click handler, will select the preset and show no defect, so the trigger is a direct test of whether the Tauri adapter delivers a genuine pointer sequence into the WebKitGTK webview. The observable is the provider form's preset field remaining unset
remaining: build the Tauri Linux artifact at both revisions
run the worker with HOME redirected into the disposable work directory so the application cannot touch a real ~/.claude or ~/.codex
reach the add-provider page without configuring any live provider, and confirm the preset list is bundled rather than fetched
prove the neighbouring legal behaviour: clicking a preset without first opening search selects it on the affected build

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the export handler passes a hardcoded defaultPath of "123.<ext>" to the Tauri dialog plugin's save(), so the native save dialog opens pre-filled with the filename 123 instead of one derived from the note's heading. The fix derives the name from the markdown content. This is the only selected defect whose observable lives outside the webview entirely: the filename entry belongs to a GTK file chooser window that Tauri opened, not to any DOM. It therefore exercises the part of the Tauri adapter that has to follow the process out of the webview and observe a separate native window, which no webview-only harness can do
remaining: build the Tauri Linux artifact at both revisions with the GTK file chooser available in the worker
confirm which file chooser backend the worker gets, because an xdg-desktop-portal chooser and the in-process GTK chooser are observed differently, and record the chosen one as a bound
seed a note whose first line is a markdown heading so the fixed build has a distinct expected filename
reach the export menu without configuring any AI provider or sync target, keeping the run offline
decide whether to observe the dialog's filename entry through AT-SPI or to accept the written file's name as the observable, and record which
